title: Rollout tactical brain dump - midweek
body:
Context:
- Quick midweek capture while ideas are still hot. Not a polished plan; more of tactical notes for the canary + UI instrumentation work.
- Participants (quick): Maya (owner), Diego (frontend), Ava (analytics), Henry (rollouts), Sam (QA on call).

Highlights from standup:
- Canary rollout for /rollouts/v2 continues. 10% traffic in region us-west-2. Latency sits ~8% higher for tail 95 (p95) vs v1 under synthetic load.
- Frontend observed a rendering jitter when KV cache fallback is hit — happens primarily when preview pane requests model metadata in parallel to token stream.
- Analytics found an uptick in aborted sessions correlated with the jitter window (spike between 14:10–14:27 PST yesterday).
- Feature flag state divergence: some accounts still hit legacy config even after flag flip (suspect stale config push on Dedicated nodes).

Observed metrics / quick queries (Ava):
- Dashboard: console-rollouts/canary-overview -> p95 latency v2: 420ms (baseline v1: 385ms)
- Aborted sessions query: SELECT COUNT(*) WHERE event = 'session_abort' AND env = 'canary' AND timestamp > now()-24h GROUP BY hour(); + showed 3x increase during jitter window.
- Error pattern: 502s from model-proxy when cache miss concurrency > 8.

Open hypotheses:
1) Rendering jitter is caused by repeated reflow when preview component rebinds to stream events; a batching debounce could hide the jitter.
2) Increased p95 is partly due to model-proxy retry storms when cache miss path hits a slow quantized model on the dedicated pool.
3) Flag divergence due to older config agent process not reloading feature-store after recent rollout (agent PID recycle needed).

Tactical experiments to run (next 48h):
- FE: Add 100ms debounce on preview stream binding, deploy behind feature flag RWD-2048. Quick AB: measure aborted sessions and reflow count. Owner: Diego. ETA: 2026-04-26.
- Infra: Force rotate config agent on 3 Dedicated nodes in canary pool, check flag propagation latency. Owner: Henry. ETA: 2026-04-24 (today, low-risk nodes).
- Runtime: Add lightweight telemetry to model-proxy for cache-miss latency buckets (<=5ms, 5-20ms, 20-100ms, >100ms). Owner: Sam (with infra). ETA: 2026-04-25.
- Analytics: Add derived metric "preview-reflow-count" from front-end instrumentation (windowed by session). Owner: Ava. ETA: 2026-04-25.

Action items (short list):
- Diego: prototype debounce and push PR -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4123 (in review).
- Ava: pin exact hours for aborted-session spike and attach CSV to ticket JIRA-RWD-2048.
- Henry: schedule node config-agent rotate, record logs, escalate if divergence persists.
- Maya: prepare rollback criteria doc (p95 delta > 10% sustained over 1h OR aborted sessions +3x baseline).

Risk matrix / rollback plan (sketch):
- Safety nets: canary traffic redirect to v1 via router policy within 2 minutes; console UI clients will fall back to legacy preview component if feature flag removed.
- Rollback triggers: sustained p95 degradation, >2% user-facing errors, or customer report linking to preview failures.
- Communication: post update to #console-rollouts and tag key customers.

Notes from QA check (Sam):
- Repro steps for jitter: 1) Open preview on a large model response (>1024 tokens), 2) trigger KV cache flush on server, 3) concurrently open second tab hitting same session id. Observed reflow in 90% of runs.
- Suggested temporary mitigation: throttle preview updates to 1 every 120ms if high concurrency detected.

Decisions and trade-offs discussed:
- We accept a mild debounce on preview updates (UX trade: slightly delayed incremental preview vs. janky layout). Prefer this short-term to reduce aborted sessions. Long-term fix: fix stream binding at component boundary.
- Not rolling back the canary immediately since errors are contained and we have quick rollback path. We proceed with telemetry + small FE change.

Questions for engineering leads:
- Is it acceptable to inject lightweight telemetry into model-proxy without a full code review cycle (temporary toggle)? (Henry to advise)
- Do we have capacity to run a small synthetic load test (10m) post-deploy to validate p95 under representative concurrency? (SRE to confirm)

Links and refs (quick):
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4123 (FE debounce)
- Jira: JIRA-RWD-2048 (preview debounce), JIRA-ENG-3456 (config agent rotation)
- Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C07ABC8/p1713648000000000 (midweek ops chatter)
- Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=987654321 (rollback criteria doc)

Quick retrospective note (to capture later):
- Need a short runbook for preview-component throttling + metrics mapping so future rollouts avoid surprises. Add to console-runbooks space.

Misc scribbles / things to save:
- Sample gauge to add: preview.render.reflows{component,env} -> counts per minute
- Query alias to add: canary_p95_vs_baseline -> (p95_canary - p95_baseline) / p95_baseline

Next sync: Friday standup quick check (2026-04-24 10:30am PST) — aim to have debounce in canary and first telemetry flush.

——
Notes end. Treat this doc as ephemeral (working). If anything looks important, convert to a ticket or add to the rollouts tracker.
action_items: Diego: push FE debounce PR and run AB test
Ava: attach aborted-session CSV to JIRA-RWD-2048
Henry: rotate config agent on 3 dedicated nodes and capture logs
Sam: add telemetry hooks to model-proxy and run quick synthetic load
summary: Midweek tactical notes capturing canary anomalies: UI rendering jitter causing aborted sessions, p95 delta higher on canary, suspected cache-miss and config-propagation causes. Short-term plan: FE debounce + telemetry + config agent rotate. Rollback criteria and safety nets defined.
